channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan's economic growth to exceed global average by 2026, IMF projects
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has released its 2026 economic growth projections for 191 countries. Uzbekistan is expected to achieve an average growth rate more than double the global average. The IMF's new economic forecasts provide a detailed outlook for various nations.

item.title: First apartments in 'Intymak' mortgage complex to be delivered soon
item.description: The head of the Presidential Administration, Kanybek Tumanbaev, inspected the 'Intymak' housing complex under construction by the State Mortgage Company. He emphasized that the premium-class apartments, priced at $1,400 per square meter through state mortgage, are superior to economy-class housing. The complex will feature ample parking, a school, kindergarten, and recreational areas.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Argentina Sign Memorandum on Aviation Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Argentina have signed a memorandum of understanding and cooperation in the field of civil aviation. The agreement aims to establish sustainable professional ties between the aviation authorities of both countries. It will facilitate the exchange of professional experience, technical knowledge, and information, expanding Kyrgyzstan's international aviation partnerships.

item.title: Pavlodar Region: Lands Valued at 115 Million Tenge Returned to State
item.description: The Prosecutor's Office of Pavlodar region has successfully recovered state-owned lands, strategically important for the development of Ekibastuz's coal industry, valued at 115 million tenge. The lands were leased to "Arman kala Limited" but were used for purposes other than intended, hindering industrial infrastructure development. The court ruled to forcibly seize the lands.

item.title: Uzbekistan Extends Customs Benefits for Light Industry Until 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan has extended customs duty exemptions on imported raw materials and components for the textile industry until early 2030. Export revenue return periods for textile companies will be extended to 365 days until January 1, 2028, with no penalties for delays. The government will also support cost reduction initiatives and subsidize artificial fiber imports.

item.title: CIA Waterboarded More Detainees Post-9/11 Than Previously Known, Documents Suggest
item.description: Newly released documents indicate the CIA waterboarded more detainees after 9/11 than previously acknowledged, possibly using a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan. While the agency admitted to waterboarding three individuals, a former translator's account suggests the practice was more common and occurred at a black site known as Salt Pit.

item.title: Uzbekistan Consumer Rights Federation Reports on Five Years of Activity
item.description: The Federation of Consumer Rights Protection Societies of Uzbekistan held a conference summarizing its 2021-2025 activities. The federation received 65,649 appeals, resolving 93.9% of them, and recovered 279.4 billion UZS in material and moral damages. Most appeals concerned trade, gas, electricity, and communal services.

item.title: Bishkek City Hall Reminds Residents of Coal Bases and Solid Fuel Prices for Winter
item.description: Bishkek City Hall has announced that coal bases are operating in the capital's districts, offering solid fuel for the upcoming winter. Prices for "Kara-Keche" coal range from 7,000 soms per ton, while "Shabyrkyul" costs 7,800 soms per ton. Various districts have different quantities of coal available.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Assures Sufficient Fuel Reserves to Meet Year-End Demand
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has sufficient reserves of gasoline and diesel fuel to meet demand until the end of the year, according to a government meeting. Officials noted that current stocks, including those in transit, are adequate. The government plans to continue subsidies and review support mechanisms for the fuel sector, addressing modernization of refineries and trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan Grants Customs Authorities Investigation Powers for Pyrotechnics Cases
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved a law granting customs authorities enhanced investigation powers for certain pyrotechnics-related offenses. This amendment to the Criminal Procedure Code aims to improve the fight against customs violations, particularly concerning undeclared goods. The law also modifies the Criminal Code regarding evasion of customs duties.

item.title: Four Civil Servants Fired in Zhambyl Region for Gambling
item.description: Four civil servants in the Zhambyl region have been dismissed for participating in gambling. One specialist transferred over 23 million tenge to a gaming account. This action violates a September 2024 law prohibiting civil servants from engaging in gambling, which is grounds for dismissal. The measures aim to prevent addiction, reduce corruption, and enhance public trust.

item.title: Two Kazatomprom Top Managers Detained for Two Months
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee announced the detention of two top managers from the national atomic company Kazatomprom. A pre-trial detention of two months was imposed on the former production director and a department manager. The detentions are related to an ongoing investigation involving former leadership of Samruk-Kazyna and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Criminal Liability for Developers Housing Unfinished Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to introduce criminal liability for developers who allow people to move into apartment buildings before they are officially commissioned. The Senate reviewed a law that will amend the Urban Planning Code, obligating clients and contractors to prevent such occupancy. This measure aims to ensure resident safety and protect property rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Fine Owners of Unregistered Domestic Animals Starting 2028
item.description: Uzbekistan will begin penalizing owners of unregistered domestic animals, including cats and dogs, from January 1, 2028. Owners must register their pets in a unified electronic database before this date. This measure aims to combat livestock theft, track diseases, and control the spread of stray animals.

item.title: EU Prepares New Defense Funding Program Amid US Uncertainty
item.description: The European Union is developing a new defense financing program worth tens of billions of euros to reduce reliance on US military capabilities. The initiative, expected in the second half of 2027, will include loans and grants. Priorities are integrated air and missile defense, intelligence, and surveillance.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Criminal Liability for Occupying Unfinished Homes
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved a law establishing criminal liability for individuals and officials who facilitate the occupation of unfinished apartment buildings. The law also amends the Urban Development Code, obligating developers to prevent such illegal settlements. This aims to protect citizens' housing rights and property.

item.title: Kazakhstan Honors Laborers in Ulytau Region's Agricultural Year-End Ceremony
item.description: In the heart of Kazakhstan, the Ulytau region celebrated its agricultural workers. The event in Zhezkazgan recognized leading farmers and specialists for their contributions to food security. Regional officials presented awards and emphasized the importance of agricultural development for employment and well-being.

item.title: Kazatomprom Reports Nine-Month Financial Results, Revenue Up 16%
item.description: Kazatomprom has released its nine-month financial report, showing consolidated revenue nearing 1.4 trillion tenge, a 16% increase year-on-year. Operational profit exceeded 560 billion tenge, with net profit around 479 billion tenge. Uranium production and sales volumes also rose by 10%.

item.title: 98-Year-Old Patient Undergoes Complex TAVI Surgery in Almaty
item.description: A complex TAVI (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) surgery was successfully performed on a 98-year-old patient at the Research Institute of Cardiology and Internal Diseases in Almaty. This procedure replaced a severely stenosed aortic valve without open-heart surgery, extending the patient's life and improving health.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes Responsibility for Illegal Precursor Trafficking
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its legal framework to combat the illegal trade of precursors and synthetic drug production. New amendments to the Criminal, Criminal Procedure, and Administrative Codes will introduce stricter penalties, including criminal liability for repeat offenses. These measures aim to protect public health and national security.

item.title: Court Detains Two Kazatomprom Figures for Two Months in Corruption Case
item.description: A court has ordered the pre-trial detention of two individuals involved in the Kazatomprom corruption case for two months. The National Security Committee stated that the decision was made to prevent pressure on potential accomplices and witnesses, and to avoid the concealment of evidence. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kazatomprom Production Director Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: The court has sanctioned the two-month arrest of Kuat Omarkov, Kazatomprom's Chief Production Director, and chief manager Baykulov. They are suspected of involvement in a corruption scheme organized by former Samruk-Kazyna management. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Chair: Nation is proactive in offering global solutions
item.description: Tanzila Narbaeva, Chair of the Senate, stated that Uzbekistan, under President Mirziyoyev, is actively pursuing reforms for a New Uzbekistan. The "Uzbekistan-2030" strategy prioritizes human dignity, focusing on income growth, education, healthcare, and rights protection. New programs aim to achieve these goals.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Mobilized citizens exempt from taxes and payments
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has reviewed a new law on mobilization. Citizens called up for military service during mobilization will be exempt from taxes and mandatory payments. The law also covers ensuring the stable operation of vital sectors and provides for deferrals for certain categories of citizens.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Law on Criminal Liability for Unpaid Customs Duties
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis has approved a bill strengthening criminal liability for non-payment of customs duties and other payments. Amendments to the Criminal Code will classify evasion of customs duties as a criminal offense. Customs authorities will also gain investigative powers for certain violations.

item.title: UN Experts Express Concern Over War Crimes Accountability in Afghanistan
item.description: UN experts have warned that halting the International Criminal Court's investigations into crimes committed in Afghanistan before 2021 deprives hundreds of thousands of victims of justice. They called the decision a "major blow" to combating impunity and urged its reversal. Justice must be equal for all victims.

item.title: UN Agencies Warn of Worsening Hunger in 16 Countries Within Six Months
item.description: A new report from UN food agencies indicates that hunger is expected to intensify in 16 countries over the next six months. Conflicts, rising fuel costs, and reduced humanitarian aid are identified as key factors exacerbating the global food crisis.

item.title: First Residents of New Tashkent to Move into Apartments by Spring 2027
item.description: The first residents of New Tashkent are expected to move into apartments by spring 2027. Apartments in the "Shark Bahori" complex will be offered with finished renovations and mortgage options. The cost per square meter ranges from 10.9 to 13.9 million soms.

item.title: Kazakh banks unite for first-ever $1.5 billion syndicated loan
item.description: Kazakh banks have collaborated for the first time to arrange a $1.5 billion syndicated loan. Halyk Bank organized the deal, which will finance the acquisition of shares in "Altın-Almas AK" by Central Asia Resources Holding Ltd. This marks the first such transaction in Kazakhstan solely involving commercial banks, demonstrating the sector's capacity for large-scale financing.

item.title: Former General Director of Kazakhstan's Freight Company Detained
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has confirmed the detention of Vladimir Petrov, former general director of "KTZ-Freight Transportation" LLP. His deputy, Kairat Kabylоv, and executive director Azamat Sembay were also detained. The committee did not provide further details on the reasons for their arrest.

item.title: Two Top Managers of Kazatomprom Arrested for Two Months
item.description: Two top managers of "Kazatomprom," the national atomic company, have been arrested for two months. The National Security Committee stated the decision was made considering the nature and severity of the alleged crimes, and to prevent interference with potential accomplices and witnesses. Investigations into the corruption case are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Phosphorus Plant Reports Significant Profit After Previous Year's Loss
item.description: The Novodzhambulsky Phosphorus Plant (NDFZ) in Kazakhstan achieved a net profit of 21.1 billion tenge in 2025, a substantial improvement from an 18.9 billion tenge loss in 2024. Revenue increased by 5.5% to 145 billion tenge, with yellow phosphorus sales dominating. Europe became the primary market, accounting for 67.8% of revenue.

item.title: Hackers Breach Major US Air Force Cloud Platform, Disrupting Operations
item.description: Unknown hackers have gained access to Cloud One, a major US Air Force cloud platform storing data on military equipment, personnel, and logistics. The breach, discovered during recent platform modernization, caused system disruptions and halted several operations. The investigation is ongoing, with the identity and full scope of the intrusion yet to be determined.

item.title: Former Heads of Kazakhstan Railways Cargo Unit Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has detained three former executives of "KTZ-Cargo" LLP on suspicion of corruption. The arrested individuals include the former general director, his deputy, and the executive director of procurement. They were detained on November 9 and 10 and subsequently remanded in custody for two months by court order.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Activist Sanjar Bokayev Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison
item.description: A court in Kazakhstan has sentenced activist Sanjar Bokayev to 10 years in prison. His nephew received a 6.6-year sentence, and his videographer a 2.5-year restriction of liberty. Dozens gathered outside the court, chanting for Bokayev's freedom after the verdict.

item.title: Three Former KTZ Executives Arrested on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has arrested three former top managers of KTZ-Cargo Transportation on corruption charges. The former general director, his deputy, and a former executive director were detained on November 9-10 and have been remanded in custody for two months. Investigations are ongoing to determine the full scope of the case.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Two New Orders for Honoring Foreign Citizens
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan has approved the establishment of two new orders designed to honor foreign citizens. These two-tiered orders will be awarded to foreign heads of state, public figures, and other citizens who have made significant contributions to developing cooperation with Uzbekistan.

item.title: Sanzhar Bokaev Sentenced to 10 Years for Embezzlement
item.description: Sanzhar Bokaev has been sentenced to 10 years in prison and a ten-year ban from public activity after being found guilty of embezzling 42.2 million tenge. The funds were allegedly misappropriated during the organization of a KazTransGas auto-rally, staging a granite slab theft, and illegal tree felling for social media videos.

item.title: Former Head of Kazakhstan Railways Cargo Division Detained for Corruption
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has confirmed the detention of the former general director of "KTZ-Cargo Transportation," his deputy, and the head of procurement. Arrests occurred in early November as part of a corruption investigation. The individuals are suspected of committing corruption offenses and will be held in custody for two months.

item.title: New Tashkent Offers Land Leases Based on Investment Size, Incentivizing Businesses
item.description: Investors in New Tashkent can obtain land plots at preferential prices, with the cost depending on the volume of construction investments. Lease rights start at $200 per square meter for projects up to $50 million, decreasing to $1 per square meter for investments over $500 million. Businesses also receive interest-free installments for up to seven years.
